0735 prior to the meeting for assistance.

 TO:  Chair and Members of the Public Safety Commission

FROM:  John N. Incontro, Police Chief

DATE:  September 19, 2022

SUBJECT:  POLICE DEPARTMENT UPDATE REPORT AUGUST 2022

BACKGROUND

Each month, the San Marino Police Department provides a brief and informational update on
crime, traffic issues, and other items of interest to the public and to the Public Safety Committee.

DISCUSSION

This report is compiled in order to inform the Public Safety Commission with essential
information regarding the department’s activity in the month of August 2022.

Detective Bureau / Investigations
As of August 31, 2022, the Detective Bureau completed the following activities:
•  4 filings were submitted to the district attorney’s office for review. DUI and drug
investigations are pending lab results prior to filing.
•  One of these cases were denied filing due to the L.A. County D.A.'s special directive
order.
•  One search warrant for a medical record was authored for an on-going investigation.

In the month of August, there were six residential burglary investigations and two attempted
residential burglaries. Three of these residents had alarms activated as the other residents did
not have alarms. There were only two residents with surveillance cameras. In one of the
attempted burglaries, a neighbor was able to take a photograph of the suspect’s vehicle.
Detectives advise LA Impact surveillance teams of the suspect’s vehicle description and
information. LA Impact has placed a tracker on the vehicle and conducted surveillance.

In one of the residential burglaries, a real estate agent located a suspicious female inside the home.
The home was vacant but staged for viewings. The suspect stated she was “squatting” inside the
residence. A lead was located based on cellular phone video of the suspect and vehicle. The
suspect’s vehicle was out of Maryland. Detectives are conducting follow up investigation at this
time.

  5
 On August 10, there were two commercial burglary investigations and one attempt commercial
burglary all within the same area. An unknown suspect shattered rear windows to the businesses
located in the 2900 block of Huntington Drive. Officers were dispatched to an audible alarm at
one location when they learned two additional businesses had rear shattered windows.
Detectives conducted follow up investigation to identify a matching suspect out of Alhambra PD’s
jurisdiction. These cases were filed for an arrest warrant on the suspect.

During this month, there were 35 FLOCK automated license plate reader alert notifications.
These notifications included misreads or vehicles not removed from the stolen vehicle database
by the originating agency. Officers pursued each notification as a possible stolen vehicle and
searched the area until otherwise notified.

The FLOCK cameras are not only a useful tool to locate stolen vehicles but have helped with
follow up investigations. Officers and Detectives are able to locate suspect vehicles by searching
vehicle images through the FLOCK database. In a grand theft from a vehicle investigation,
Detectives located a vehicle matching the suspect vehicle description through FLOCK camera
images. The suspect took two purses from the victim’s vehicle. LA Impact was able to place a
tracker on the vehicle and is continuing to build a case in assisting with apprehending suspects.

Our analysis indicates generally suspects enter the rear yard through unlock pedestrian gates to
make entry in the rear of residences. This information will assist us in our crime prevention
efforts. The police department recently sent out a notification to the community regarding
burglary prevention tips. Proper lighting, alarm systems, surveillance cameras and locking doors /
gates will reduce burglaries.

  6
 Community Engagement
The month of August, the Department held our largest community engagement event, National
Night Out. A birthday party was held at the Police Station on August 13th for two certificate
winners. The department will be hosting “Coffee with a Cop” at Starbucks on October 5th, 2022
at 8 AM.

Personnel
The Police Department currently has 28 sworn positions filled. (The Police Department recently
lost two of our more tenured officers due to the vaccine mandate.) We continue to pursue
interested police officer applicants, to fill these recently vacated positions. We have two lateral
police officer candidates in the background process. There are still three cadet position vacancies.
We currently have two cadet applicants in the background process.

During the past several months, City Staff has been working with other city officials and members
of the San Gabriel Valley Council of Governments (SGVCOG) to coordinate the deployment of
a Mobile Crisis Team (MCT) to the City of San Marino, as well as the City of Arcadia and South
Pasadena. The MCT will initially be co-responding with police personnel to calls relating to mental
health emergencies or people who are unhoused. The police officers and MCT will work together
to de-escalate situations and find resources for people in need. The MCT’s response is currently
limited to dates / times they are assigned to each city, as well as limited flex hours. The MCT’s
launch date in San Marino was on Monday, August 15th. The MCT’s contacts with people suffering
from mental health emergencies in the City of San Marino have been very limited, as many of the
calls for service have occurred outside of the days / hours that the MCT is working.

Technology
Police Department Staff and I.T. are working with Performa Labs, Inc. to complete the
development portion of the training software deployment. We expect the training software to
be operational by next month.

The fourth quarter of the Office of Traffic Safety – OTS grant will end in September. Staff has
been working with various vendors to make sure that the new grant funded e-citation software
/ writers / printers and crash-reporting software will all be fully functional in the coming weeks.
This software will help Police Department Staff save time and resources, while making reporting
more timely.

Traffic
Officer Richardson and Officer Avington are our two newest Motor Officers. Pre-academy
training will begin on September 19, 2022. They will be attending the Anaheim Police Motor
Academy on November 1st and are expected to graduate November 18th.

Traffic Enforcement
Traffic enforcement is based upon three categories; traffic complaints from the community,
observation of violations by officers, and traffic collision data. The Department maintains a list of
traffic complaint locations and traffic collision data for traffic enforcement. As part of our traffic
collision investigations, we will look for other issues that may have been a contributory factor in
the collision. Those factors could be distracted driving, engineering, or environmental.

 CITY ATTORNEY'S IMPARTIAL ANALYSIS OF VACANCY TAX MEASURE __

The City of San Marino does not currently impose a tax specifically directed at vacant property. This
measure would impose a special tax on specified vacant property in the City, and use the tax revenue solely
for purposes specified in the measure.

The tax rate would be $10,000 annually for each of the following: a vacant single-family residential parcel,
a vacant residential parcel with 6 or fewer units, a vacant residential unit located on a residential parcel with
7 or more units, a vacant condominium, a vacant townhome, and a vacant ground floor unit of a building
located on a parcel on which commercial activities are allowed by applicable zoning (defined as a
“commercial space”). A single-family residential parcel, a condominium, a townhome, a residential unit
located on a residential parcel with 7 or more units, and a commercial space would each be treated as vacant
if unoccupied, uninhabited, or unused for more than 245 days in a calendar year. A multifamily residential
parcel with 6 units or less is treated as vacant where all units are unoccupied, uninhabited, or unused for
more than 245 days in a calendar year.

The measure provides a number of exemptions from the tax, e.g., exemptions for persons kept from normal
work or business activities for at least 30 days as a result of a medical event; owners who can demonstrate
certain hardships; owners of properties under construction, or for which an active building permit is being
processed, or for which a substantially complete planning application has not yet received approval; owners
of properties uninhabitable for at least 120 days during the calendar year; owners of properties who were
placed in a long-term care facility; owners of properties that were actively marketed for lease or sale during
the calendar year; and owners of properties for which 100% of their legal interest has been transferred in
the calendar year.

The measure would authorize the City Council to adopt ordinances to provide supplemental exemption
definitions; for the administration of the exemptions; and in any manner that (1) does not increase the tax
rates, or otherwise constitute a tax increase for which voter approval is required by applicable law, or (2)
does not extend the expiration date of the tax.

Revenue from the tax would be placed in a restricted fund, could be used only for the purposes stated in the
measure, and would be subject to an annual, independent audit. Permitted uses include public safety
services (including police, fire protection, and code enforcement), maintenance of school facilities and
school staffing. Tax revenue also could be used to pay the costs of an independent third-party audit of the
use of monies in the restricted fund and to pay for the costs of administering the tax.

The tax would expire automatically 10 years after it is first imposed.

The San Marino City Council placed this measure on the ballot. A two-thirds vote in support is required to
pass the measure.

JOSEPH M. MONTES
City Attorney

TO:  Chair and Members of the Public Safety Commission

FROM:  M. D. Rueda, Fire Chief

DATE:  September 19, 2022

SUBJECT:  FIRE DEPARTMENT MONTHLY REPORT

BACKGROUND

The San Marino Fire Department completes a monthly report for the Public Safety Commission,
providing an overview of department activities, significant incidents, and monthly statistics.

DISCUSSION

Monthly Performance Report
The August Performance Report for the San Marino Fire Department has been temporarily
delayed. The Fire Department is in the process of working with Verdugo to correct a number
of incorrect turnout and response times being reported. Verdugo has estimated the issue should
be fixed by the week of September 19.

Personnel
The Fire Department conducted interviews during the week of September 5 for the position of
firefighter/paramedic. The department currently has one vacancy due to a firefighter/paramedic
accepting a position with another department. One candidate was successfully moved forward
to the next step of the recruitment process.

San Marino Motor Classic
San Marino Fire Department provided additional staffing at the San Marino Motor Classic on
Sunday, August 28. Two firefighter/paramedics and a Command Officer were assigned the event.
The firefighter/paramedics were assigned to a medcart on loan from the San Gabriel Fire
Department for the duration of the event. The medcart allows firefighter/paramedics to respond
to medical emergencies where large crowds would prohibit quick response by the rescue
ambulance. The San Marino Fire Department received approval to purchase its own medcart as
part of the current fiscal year’s capital equipment budget. Frontline RA91 and E91 remained
available to respond to incidents occurring in the City. One patient during the event required
assistance from RA91 for transport to a local area hospital.

The Fire Department provided emergency management training to executive team members
prior to Sunday’s car show. The training focused on a potential multi-casualty incident occurring
at the Lacy Park venue.
 Significant Incidents
On August 9, the Fire Department responded to a structure fire on the 2400 block of Ridgeway
Road. Chiefs Rueda and Dondanville were first on scene, having observed the smoke from the
Fire Department’s front apron. The two Chiefs alerted the department’s dispatch center and
began fire extinguishment efforts. Engine 91 was dispatched to the incident along with engines
from the Alhambra Pasadena, and San Gabriel Fire Departments. After the fire was successfully
extinguished, San Marino fire investigators determined the probable cause was due to
construction occurring on the property.

On September 4, Engine 91 responded to major flooding conditions on the 1100 block of Adair
Street. Firefighters successfully evacuated the water from the home’s basement. Mindful of
current water restrictions, Engineer White redirected the runoff away from the street and
instead watered the vegetation in the property’s front yard.

On September 4, Engine 91 responded to investigate a hazard on the 2200 block of Oak Knoll.
An oak tree in the rear of the property fell, causing damage to the roof and knocking down wires.
Although the power lines were intact, there was no power to the house and E91 was unable to
shut down utilities due to their location under the fallen tree. Southern California Edison and
the City of San Marino Community Development department were notified. E91 remained on
scene until an electrician arrived.

San Marino Engine 91 was dispatched on September 7 as part of Strike Team 1202A to the
Fairview Incident in Riverside County. Two engines from Burbank and two engines from Glendale
were also dispatched as part of the response. As a result of the change in weather and improved
control lines on the Fairview Incident, Engine 91 and the Strike Team 1202A was reassigned by
the State to the Mosquito Incident in Placer County. As of September 15, the Mosquito Fire
Incident is a 64,159 acre wildfire stretching over two counties, El Dorado and Placer
Counties. The fire has been burning eight days. As with other requests by the State, this
deployment is 110% reimbursable, and standby personnel are staffing our reserve engine in our
City. The Strike Team may be deployed up to 14 days.

FY 2022-23 Department Objectives
  • Complete the Lexipol implementation of fire department policies and procedures.
  • Accept delivery of the new RA 91.
  • Conduct a review of the current Community Emergency Response Training (CERT) and
  develop a “Citizen Fire Academy” for residents’ participation.
  • Conduct Fire Department First Aid Community Instructional Workshops.
  • Begin construction on the Fire Department’s bathroom renovation.
  • Develop and conduct emergency operations, active shooter training partnered with a
  consultant and the Huntington Library staff.
  • Present the City’s revised Emergency Operations Plan to the Disaster Council and City
  Council for approval.
  • Update the City’s Disaster Cache Inventory.
  • Complete the EOC upgrade.
 RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends the Commission receive and file the Fire Department Monthly Report. If the
Commission concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

“I move to receive and file the Fire Department Monthly Report.”

 TO:  Chair Boegh and members of the Public Safety Commission

FROM:  Robert Newman, Interim Director of Parks & Public Works/City Engineer

DATE:  September 19, 2022

SUBJECT:  AUGUST THROUGH SEPTEMBER PARKS AND PUBLIC WORKS
  UPDATE

BACKGROUND

Please accept the following as a summary of notable activities that have been accomplished, are
underway or are planned for the balance of this month through your next regularly scheduled
commission meeting.

DISCUSSION

Follow-up Items from Prior Commission Meetings
•  The Citywide Traffic Circulation Study, for which the City awarded a contract to the traffic
  consultant Iteris, was originally reviewed by the Public Safety Commission in July 2021, and
  brought before the City Council in October 2021. At that meeting, the City Council
  requested that Iteris include additional information such as improvement prioritization, near-
  term 2023 analysis, collision data “hotspot” review, and additional conceptual designs for the
  intersection of Huntington Drive at Sierra Madre Boulevard/San Marino Avenue. The Council
  then voted to remand the draft study back to the Public Safety Commission for review once
  these tasks were completed and changes were incorporated into the draft report. In early
  2022, the Parks and Public Works Department conducted a residential survey to gain
  additional resident input into traffic safety concerns. The data from this survey was shared
  with Iteris to assist them in developing recommendations and completing their report. Staff
  recently reached out to Iteris to get a progress update and timeline for when the completed
  report would be ready for the Commission to review. During this meeting, they indicated
  that they anticipate this study will be ready to share with the Commission later this year.
•  Striping modifications on Huntington Drive westbound between Monterey Road and
  Westhaven Road is still under review by the City’s traffic engineer. A design is expected to
  be shared with the Commission at a future meeting.

  14
 Projects in or near Construction
•  Mariposa Landscaping has continued its scheduled work in its Multi-Year Tree Maintenance
  Contract for FY 22-23. To this point, they have planted approximately 70 new trees at
  various locations throughout the City, performed removal of trees approved by the City
  Council, trimmed palm trees citywide, trimmed trees at Lacy Park in preparation for the 4th
  of July celebration, performed grid trimming of right-of-way trees north of Huntington Drive
  from Virginia Road westbound to City limits, and completed additional raise pruning of trees
  to ensure adequate clearance for Fire Department vehicles. Mariposa’s seasonal tree
  trimming/pruning is complete for the time being.
•  Construction for this fiscal year’s street rehabilitation program project is underway. The
  City’s contractor, All American Asphalt, has begun replacing curb and gutter on some of the
  identified streets. A total of 31 City streets are scheduled to be resurfaced as part of the
  project based on the Council-adopted pavement management plan. The restriping work on
  Sierra Madre Boulevard that was previously discussed at a Commission meeting has been
  incorporated into the project’s scope of work, and will take place at a later point in the
  project. Work is expected to be completed by mid-November.
•  Construction for the FY 22-23 sidewalk replacement program is expected to begin later in
  the fall, after the conclusion of the Street Rehabilitation project. This program replaces
  approximately 1.0 mile of sidewalk each year at various locations throughout the City.
•  At its July 29th meeting, the City Council awarded a construction contract to CABD
  Construction, as well as a construction management contract to Griffin Structures for the
  San Marino Center Renovation. A ceremonial groundbreaking is scheduled for Thursday,
  September 29th, with construction activities scheduled to begin later this month.
Projects in Design/Out-to-Bid

•  The Department received a request to study the signage on West Drive at Sherwood Road
  and at Lorain Road for the purposes of highlighting pedestrian activity at these intersections.
  The Department has updated several signs with the current labeling and colors for signs and
  has completed the refreshing of existing ladder crosswalk striping in the near future.
•  Rubio Medina Architects, the consultant for the Fire Station Bathroom Remodel Project, has
  continued their design work on the project.
•  Dudek engineers continue to work on the plans to upgrade of our 3 sanitary sewer lift stations
  as part of the lift station improvement program. They are at the 95% design plans stage.
  Advertisement for construction bids is planned for later this year.

  15
 Projects under Study/Analysis

•  The Department has been placing W11-15 signs (see nearby) along certain

 TO:  Chair and Members of the Public Safety Commission

FROM:  John N. Incontro, Police Chief

DATE:  September 19, 2022

SUBJECT:  CARRYING A CONCEALED WEAPON PERMIT PROCESS

BACKGROUND

The Department is currently reviewing the current policy regarding CCW permits and will be
accepting applications in the near future.

DISCUSSION

Carrying a Concealed Weapon Permit Process
In June, the United States Supreme Court struck down New York state’s concealed carry
permitting law, New York State Rifle and Pistol Association INC. et al v. Bruen, Superintendent
of the New York State Police et al., which is very similar to California’s and which gave local law
enforcement discretion to determine who should be allowed to carry a concealed handgun in
public. Local Police Chiefs and County Sheriffs had utilized a rule that required an applicant to
show good cause to receive a concealed carry permit. On June 24, Attorney General Rob Bonta
advised all county sheriffs and police chiefs in the state that they “may no longer require a
demonstration of ‘good cause’ in order to obtain a concealed carry permit.” Now, an applicant
must have “good moral character” along with other requirements to carry a concealed handgun.
California law requires applicants to undergo a background check, take a safety course, and satisfy
a “good moral character” standard, often interpreted to disqualify those who have committed
violent felonies or are the subject of restraining orders.

The Police Department has the responsibility of receiving requests for Concealed Carry Permits
from those individuals who are residents of the City. The City is currently evaluating the new
process that includes the following from the SCOTUS decision:

•  The Supreme Court did not hold that a state cannot require a license to carry a firearm
in public.
•  California still regulates the carrying of firearms in public places, in part, by requiring a
license to "carry concealed a pistol, revolver, or other firearm capable of being concealed upon
the person."
 •  California laws forbidding the carrying of firearms in sensitive places such as schools and
government buildings, even with a license are still in effect.
•  Private businesses and property owners can still regulate whether firearms can be brought
into their establishments or onto their property.

Individuals requesting a permit must:
•  Complete an application, with proof of residency
•  Complete a gun safety training course
•  Undergo a psychological test
•  Must be eligible to possess a handgun
•  Successfully complete and pass a background investigation

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends the Commission receive and file the carrying a concealed weapon permit
process report. If the Commission concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion
would be:

“I move to receive and file the carrying a concealed weapon permit process report.”
